newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-TEENAGER HENRY SHINES AS MONACO GO TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TEENAGER HENRY SHINES AS MONACO GO TOP.

text.p: Two goals by teenager Thierry Henry helped Monaco crush Bordeaux 3-1 and take them to the top of the French first division on Saturday.
Monaco joined Paris St Germain on 29 points but jumped above them thanks to a better goal difference. The Paris club meet Bastia at Parc des Princes on Sunday.
Monaco went ahead after just eight minutes with a headed goal by midfielder Sylvain Legwinski. A brilliant strike by 19-year-old Henry just before halftime left Bordeaux with a mountain to climb.
Henry, who is understood to be attracting the interest of several big European clubs including Real Madrid, put the issue beyond doubt with his second goal in the 65th minute.
Bordeaux, who have not won in Monaco for 15 years, reduced the arrears with a goal by Ibrahim Ba six minutes later.
Champions Auxerre won 2-0 at Le Havre to remain in third place one point behind Monaco and PSG.

"We played far better than we did on Wednesday," said Auxerre trainer Guy Roux, referring to his side's 3-1 defeat by Grasshopper Zurich in the Champions' League. "We're just behind the leading teams and that's excellent."
Alain Goma headed Auxerre in front in the 23rd minute. Algerian midfielder Moussa Saib scored the second eight minutes from time.
Former European champions Marseille plunged deeper into a crisis which could cost trainer Gerard Gili his job by losing 2-0 in Montpellier. They trail Monaco by 12 points.
Marseille were reduced to 10 men when Italian central defender Alberto Malusci was sent off for a second bookable offence just before halftime.
Ivory Coast striker Ibrahim Bakayoko scored twice for Montpellier, in the 10th and 46th minutes.
